q: What is the actual causal mechanism driving the KL47->KL64 serotype replacement — recombination of the wzc CD1-VR2-CD2 region as Zhang et al. hypothesize, host/antibiotic selection on plasmid-borne rmpA/iuc virulence, healthcare-network founder effects (few super-spreader ST11-KL64 lineages exported worldwide), or a combination?
basis: The paper claims a ~303bp wzc VR2 recombination 'facilitates' the KL47->KL64 transition (Section 3.5) and explicitly names as a limitation 'no related experiments performed to demonstrate the effect of recombination of particular region fragments on the transformation of KL47 into KL64' (Section 4). Our replication independently confirms the epidemiological transition (KL64 crossover in 2016, KL64 rmpA 29.1% vs KL47 2.3%, +12.7x) but cannot distinguish 'wzc recombination caused the takeover' from 'a KL64 clone with a virulence plasmid was clonally exported.' No wet-lab knockout / swap has ever been done. The 386-genome tree and the 955-genome dataset both cluster ST11-KL64 tightly, consistent with clonal expansion rather than repeated independent KL47->KL64 conversion.
next_steps: (1) Reconstruct the KL64 sub-phylogeny (Roary core-genome + IQ-TREE) on the 413 ST11-KL64 assemblies we have on uicgpu; measure monophyly and estimate the number of independent KL47->KL64 conversion events using ancestral-state reconstruction (BEAST or TreeTime); a monophyletic KL64 clade would falsify the 'recombination drives repeated conversions' story and support 'single clonal export.' (2) Formally test the wzc-swap hypothesis by lambda-Red allelic exchange of the KL47 wzc CD1-VR2-CD2 region into a KL64 backbone (and vice versa) in a laboratory K. pneumoniae strain, then assay capsule serotype, in-vitro macrophage survival, and mouse virulence; this is the direct experiment the paper explicitly flags as missing. (3) Search BV-BRC and NCBI for ST11 isolates carrying the KL64 wzc VR2 but a KL47-like plasmid content (or vice versa) to test whether wzc genotype and virulence-plasmid content are separable — if they always co-segregate, plasmid selection could be the primary driver, not wzc recombination.

q: Has KL64 dominance saturated, reversed, or been overtaken by a new K-locus (e.g. KL24, KL105) in the post-2020 CRKP population, and are new carbapenemases (blaNDM-5, OXA-232) replacing blaKPC-2 in these emerging serotypes?
basis: The paper's window ends in 2020. Our 2020 slice has only n=14 ST11 CRKP genomes (submissions collapsed post-COVID), so we CANNOT test whether the KL47->KL64 curve has plateaued or begun another shift. We independently observe KL24 (14.2%, n=135) and KL105 (6.6%, n=63) as the third and fourth ST11 K-loci — neither is emphasized by Zhang et al. — and rising minority carbapenemases blaNDM-1 (13.9%, vs paper's ~7%), blaOXA-48 (6.4% vs ~4%), and previously-unmentioned OXA-232 (1.0%). This is a live public-health question with treatment implications: ceftazidime-avibactam covers KPC but not NDM/OXA-48-like enzymes.
next_steps: (1) Extend the BV-BRC pull to 2021-2026 (already-implemented pipeline in `data/` scripts; incremental run) and repeat the Kleborate v3.2.4 pass on the ~1000-2000 new ST11 CRKP genomes; produce the same year-by-year K-locus and carbapenemase tables and check for slope change after 2020. (2) Cross-check against WHO GLASS 2023-2024 CRKP reports and the CHINET surveillance publications (both post-date the paper) to see if the field-level trend agrees with the BV-BRC signal. (3) Specifically profile the KL24 and KL105 ST11 sub-populations for virulence plasmid content (rmpA, iuc) and carbapenemase mix — if either is accumulating hypervirulence markers, it may be the next serotype-of-concern the field has to watch.

q: How large is the metadata-selection bias between what Zhang et al. analyzed (386 ST11 CRKP, filtered on 8 specific human sample sources) and what a modern BV-BRC pull actually returns (955 ST11 CRKP, sample-site metadata missing for 92%), and does the KL47->KL64 conclusion survive when properly controlled for country/sample-source/year confounders?
basis: Our replication cannot apply the paper's 8-sample-source filter because BV-BRC's `body_sample_site` field is empty for 92% of Klebsiella pneumoniae records — this is the single largest methodological gap in the replication and it is a database-side missing-data problem, not one Zhang et al. can fix. China contributes 61% of our ST11 CRKP and 64.5% of theirs; if the KL64 signal is largely a Chinese hospital-network signal, then 'global KL47->KL64 transition' is potentially overstated. The paper does not stratify the KL47/KL64 crossover by country or sample source, so we cannot tell from the paper alone whether the trend holds outside Chinese blood isolates.
next_steps: (1) Scrape isolation-source metadata directly from NCBI BioSample for the 955 ST11 CRKP genome accessions (each BV-BRC genome links back to a BioSample) using Entrez efetch on `biosample_accession`; fill the 92%-missing `body_sample_site` field; this recovers the paper's inclusion criterion for a modern dataset. (2) Re-run the KL47->KL64 crossover analysis stratified by country (China vs non-China) and, once metadata is recovered, by sample source, using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test to hold confounders fixed. (3) Contact Zhang et al. (chenyonger@126.com per the paper) and request their curated genome-inclusion table as supplementary data — the paper cites Supplementary Table S1 but our audit shows the deposited version does not contain the sample-source filter decisions.

q: Which specific mobile genetic elements (IS26, ISKpn6/7, ICEKp10, IncFIB/IncHI1B plasmids) are actually transporting the rmpA/iuc virulence loci into the ST11-KL64 background, and does the emerging convergent 'hypervirulent + carbapenem-resistant' (hv-CRKP) phenotype have a common vehicle that could be targeted for surveillance?
basis: The paper reports the differential presence of rmpA/rmpA2, iucABCD, and iutA between KL47 and KL64 (Table 3; 35 of 134 VFDB genes p<0.05) and speculates that recombination is responsible, but does NOT identify the mobile-element vehicle or the plasmid backbone. Our Kleborate v3.2.4 replication confirms the direction (rmpA +26.8 percentage points in KL64, clb +9.0 pp, iuc +5.8 pp) but Kleborate loci-level detection does not resolve genomic context. The clinical significance is huge: convergent hv-CRKP has been documented as causing outbreaks with >50% mortality (Gu et al. 2018, Lancet Infect Dis) and any actionable surveillance requires knowing which plasmid or IS element to flag.
next_steps: (1) Long-read (Nanopore or PacBio) resequence a panel of ~30 representative KL64 rmpA+ isolates and ~10 KL47 rmpA+ isolates from the 955-genome set, then assemble with Flye/Unicycler and identify plasmid replicons with PlasmidFinder + mob_suite; compare plasmid backbones and MGE flanking regions of rmpA. (2) On the existing short-read assemblies, run ISfinder/ISEScan and CONJscan to catalogue MGEs in a 5-kb window around rmpA, rmpA2, iucABCD; test whether IS26 or ICEKp10 flanks are enriched in KL64 vs KL47. (3) Publish an rmpA-vehicle typing scheme (analogous to `Kleborate --min_kpsc_mash_score`) so downstream surveillance labs can rapidly flag not just 'rmpA present' but 'rmpA on ICEKp10-like element' — this converts an epidemiological observation into an actionable clinical alert.

q: How much of the reported 'differential virulence between KL47 and KL64' is real biology versus artefacts of database growth, sequencing-platform heterogeneity, and per-genome assembly quality — and can the KL47->KL64 finding be reproduced blind on independently-assembled reads (SRA -> denovo assembly) rather than on BV-BRC's precomputed public assemblies?
basis: Both the paper and our replication use PATRIC/BV-BRC's pre-deposited assemblies, whose quality varies wildly (Illumina 100bp reads through PacBio HiFi, N50 from 5kb to complete). Kleborate is sensitive to assembly fragmentation for the wzc/K-locus call: a partial K-locus can be miscalled as an unrelated KL type. Our replication has NOT audited per-genome assembly quality (contig count, N50, BUSCO completeness) or filtered on it. Furthermore, BV-BRC has grown ~2.5x for ST11 CRKP since the 2022 PATRIC snapshot (955 vs 386), and if the new submissions are systematically biased toward large Chinese KL64 outbreak studies (a plausible sampling bias), our proportion estimates may be biased upward for KL64 in a way that is invisible to us. This is a validity threat to both papers.
next_steps: (1) For each of the 955 assemblies, compute contig count, total length, N50, and CheckM completeness; filter to a high-quality subset (>=95% BUSCO complete, N50 >= 30kb, total length 5-6.5 Mb) and re-run Kleborate; check whether the KL47->KL64 proportions and rmpA/iuc differentials survive the filter. (2) Take 100 randomly-chosen BV-BRC ST11 CRKP isolates for which raw SRA reads are available, re-assemble de novo with Unicycler / Trycycler (uicgpu has the compute), re-run Kleborate on the fresh assemblies, and compare K-locus/virulence calls to the BV-BRC precomputed ones — quantify the concordance rate. (3) Simulate a 'no growth' counterfactual: sub-sample the 955-genome set down to the 386 pre-2022 accessions and re-run the analysis; if the KL47->KL64 crossover and effect sizes are preserved on the exact same isolates the paper used, database-growth confounding is ruled out.
